So many @sagaftra members in RI and across the country struggle to afford necessities like health care, groceries, and housing.

I’m fighting in Congress to ensure all workers can exercise their rights to unionize and earn fair contracts. https://t.co/mylhgrBf9F

Dog owners: make sure you are taking the necessary precautions to protect your four-legged friend from illness that has appeared in many states, including Rhode Island. ⤵️
https://t.co/kpFRcs7t72
Thank you to @HSLegFund for the perfect score on your 2023 Legislative Scorecard. I will keep fighting for our furry friends and the humane treatment of animals nationwide. 🐕🐈 https://t.co/AQTMt5Fb6J

Everyone deserves respect & equal treatment under the law.  At a time when too many politicians target and attack members of the LGBTQ+ community, I was pleased to hold the first meeting of my RI02 LGBTQ+ advisory committee as we work to build a future where everyone is valued. https://t.co/QvmWhQxkXU

Every 5 years Congress passes a #FarmBill covering a wide range of issues, from crop insurance to nutrition programs.
 
The bill is up for renewal this year & we must use this opportunity to lower costs for working people, strengthen American agriculture & fight food insecurity.

Many families in RI rely on Head Start for early childhood education, health care and nutrition, yet Congressional Republicans want to cut funding for this essential program.

Families deserve better. Standing with @NatlHeadStart this morning to say: we’re fighting back! https://t.co/uXIU2l8pTp

This week the House is voting on a bill aimed at halting the flow of fentanyl. Good.

I am introducing amendments to ensure that grants for addiction treatment are not frozen by Trump/Musk and to make it harder for cartels to get their hands on American-made guns.

My amendments to protect addiction treatment funding from being cut & to stop American guns from arming cartels were BLOCKED by House R’s.

Disappointing. Beating fentanyl takes putting partisan politics aside.

Read more about my proposals ⬇️

https://t.co/FD3uNgOSpO

Trump’s plan for the U.S. to take control of Gaza is reckless & immoral. We cannot risk US lives on yet another nation building exercise, especially one that would mean the forced displacement of millions of people.

I'm joining 144 of my colleagues to stand in opposition.

READ: https://t.co/BM6NhddCgu

Great meeting with the National Bleeding Disorders Foundation to talk about protecting access to life-saving care.

Every Rhode Islander deserves the treatment they need, and I’m working to make sure those with bleeding disorders aren’t left behind. https://t.co/ZcgTsW9wjA

Daylight Saving Time begins this weekend! ⏰ Losing an hour of sleep is never fun, but some say longer evenings are worth it. 

What do you think?

💡 Keep Daylight Saving Time year-round
🌅 Stick to Standard Time year-round
🔄 Keep changing the clocks

Rhode Island has one of the highest MS diagnosis rates in the US—and if you or a loved one has it, you know how tough it can be.

I sat down with Rhode Islanders from the Multiple Sclerosis Society in DC to talk about how we can team up to deliver better care and more support. https://t.co/K9GM3QqlPD

Day 2. I’m speaking out on the House floor every session day until @EdesiaNutrition’s funding is restored.

Edesia’s US-made emergency nutrition has reached 25M+ children in crisis, arriving in a box stamped: From the American People.

This is patriotism—and it’s at risk. https://t.co/gGiyXt0Dg0

Day 11. Still speaking out every day until Trump restores funding for lifesaving food aid.

But today, I rise with a glimmer of hope: Edesia just got an order to ship nutrition to kids in Sudan. We’re not done yet, but this is an important first step. https://t.co/hQCJiAVPdP

Good news: following our advocacy, this girl has been granted permission to stay and continue treatment.

A victory for decency, but this is just a start. The Trump administration should not be deporting any sick children against their will, period.

Another week has passed, and Edesia Nutrition still hasn’t had its funding restored. I took the House floor each day again.

Children are dying.

The Trump administration says help is coming, but there’s been no action.

It's time to act. https://t.co/l3e3z844CZ

Yesterday, a bipartisan group of congressional staff from across the country visited Edesia Nutrition in North Kingstown.

Congress has long supported manufacturers like Edesia for their lifesaving work feeding children around the world. https://t.co/DJqFU2rnyg

I visited the Edesia Nutrition Factory in North Kingstown over the weekend.

It is long past time that the Trump administration honor its word and get the shipments moving again. https://t.co/CjRF1yZP1e

Cancer touches nearly every family. 

I am committed to advancing policies that improve prevention, treatment, and access to affordable care.

Thank you @ACSCAN for your tireless advocacy and support for those fighting cancer. https://t.co/P21nXRgYBd

The 80% of Americans who want health care funding in the budget are not “terrorists”, they are every people who can’t afford for their premiums to double.

Stop whining and call a vote on a budget that includes health care funding. It’s that simple.

1 in 4 Rhode Islanders over 65 experienced a fall last year. Falls are preventable and deadly if ignored.

I am proud to cosponsor the SAFE Act of 2025 to add fall-risk screenings and prevention to Medicare wellness visits to help keep seniors safe. https://t.co/qdSwjQHzW6

Health care costs are skyrocketing right now.

In my home state of RI, insurers announced double-digit rate hikes for next year, and open enrollment starts November 1.

That’s when families make choices about coverage, and hospitals set their budgets. They can’t afford to wait. https://t.co/lGjlavqOV0

People, and our entire health care system, can’t wait another day.

People are already doing the math on what these rising premiums mean for their budgets. Hospitals and Drs Offices are bracing for the fallout.

This is urgent.

Susan’s health insurance costs will go up by $1,100 per month if Republicans in Congress let the Affordable Care Act tax credits expire.

Her story, and millions more like it, is why we must include health care funding in the budget. https://t.co/QTq7ZEfNy3

Hundreds of billions of Medicaid cuts & the expiration of ACA tax credits are a ‘one-two punch’ to RI's health care system.

Hospitals and patients can’t afford this. 

We need urgent action to fix the health care crisis as part of any budget agreement. https://t.co/CbXzsQ9adE
